To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a multilevel bang–bang CDR has superior performance compared to an Alexander type multilevel PD based CDR in the presence of intersymbol interference and additive white Gaussian noise.
the bang-bang CDM is more tolerant to ISI and noise at large ISI and small signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) compared to the Alexander type multilevel CDR.
a stochastic analysis is employed to model a multilevel bangbang CDR and that it is shown that the bang-bang CDF outperforms the Alexander PD based CDR in the presence of large ISI and low SNR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modeling and design of multilevel CDRs in presence of ISI and additive noise.
the modeling and design of multilevel clock-and data-recovery systems.
the design of multilevel bang bang clock recovery circuits for optical communications.

the stochastic approach provides a useful tool for modeling and designing CDRs in a wide variety of scenarios, and that it is possible to design CDRs that perform better than the conventional Alexander type CDRs.
